DER developers and aggregators SSTs can help DER developers and aggregators to better integrate their products into the grid. They can convert DC to AC and vice versa and contribute to voltage and frequency regulation. SSTs can help energy storage systems provide grid services, such as frequency regulation and peak shaving. This can help increase the reliability of renewable energy sources and make them more attractive to utilities. SSTs can help DER aggregators improve the performance of their systems, by providing faster response times and more precise control over power flow. This can help DER aggregators optimize the use of DERs, improve system reliability, and potentially increase revenue from ancillary services and demand response programs. 15 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. SST benefits to Balancing Authorities 1. Improved grid stability and reliability: SSTs provide voltage and frequency regulation that improves grid stability and reliability. This is important for balancing authorities, as they are responsible for ensuring the real-time balance of supply and demand. 2. Increased grid flexibility: SSTs can enable the integration of renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind, into the grid. This can help balancing authorities meet their renewable energy targets and reduce their reliance on fossil fuels. SSTs can also help balance the grid during periods of high demand, by providing reactive power support and reducing the need for expensive peaking power plants. 3. Reduced maintenance and repair costs: SSTs have fewer moving parts and are more durable than traditional transformers. This can help reduce the need for maintenance and repairs, which can be costly for balancing authorities. Thus, SSTs can provide long-term cost savings despite higher initial costs. 4. Improved efficiency: SSTs are generally more efficient than traditional transformers, particularly when it comes to converting power from DC to AC or vice versa. This can help balancing authorities reduce their energy losses and improve overall grid efficiency. Benefits to customers SSTs can improve power quality for industrial and commercial customers, leading to increased efficiency and productivity. They can also help reduce downtime and maintenance costs, as they are less likely to fail than traditional transformers. SSTs can potentially lead to lower electricity costs for consumers, as they can improve grid efficiency and reduce the need for expensive upgrades to the grid infrastructure. Task 4 Perform system level simulations and value analysis: In this task, the system level simulations are performed by NREL team for a range of use cases defined the previous tasks including “corridor charging” for EVs and solar plus storage (FERC 2222). The test data collected from the simulations will be used as an input to the SST value analysis. Visualizations are developed as needed to develop insights into the data.
